We created a visualization tool, called Circos, to facilitate the identification and analysis of similarities and differences arising from comparisons of genomes.
Circos is effective in displaying variation in genome structure and any other kind of positional relationships between genomic intervals.

The recommended method uses a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework.
RAG consists of two stages: a retriever and a generator.
The retriever takes the user’s query and maps both the query and documents from an external corpus into a high-dimensional vector space using a shared embedding model.
The retriever identifies the most relevant documents by calculating similarities (e.g., Euclidean distance) between the query vector and document vectors.
The generator, often a pre-trained large language model (LLM), uses the content of retrieved documents to produce natural language text that satisfies both syntactic and semantic requirements.
The prompt input to the generator is optimized through prompt engineering to guide the model in generating the most relevant output.
